# Juniper SRX Routing, Interfaces and Traffic

_Juniper SRX · 27 commands_

The Junos operational commands you need when an SRX acts as a router. Routes, interfaces, OSPF/BGP, sessions, and safe changes with commit confirmed.

Legend: » show · ✎ config · ► action · ↺ clear · ◆ rarely used gem · ▲ caution · ↑ version added

| | Command | What it does | Mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| » | `show route <prefix> [exact] [table <instance>.inet.0]` | The routing table entry for a prefix. Shows the active route (*), protocol, preference and next hop. | operational |
| » | `show route summary` | The number of routes per table and protocol. A quick sanity check after a change. | operational |
| » | `show route protocol <static \| ospf \| bgp \| direct> [table <table>]` | Only the routes of one protocol. | operational |
| » | `show route <prefix> extensive` | Everything about a route, including all paths, why one was chosen and the BGP attributes. | operational |
| » | `show route forwarding-table destination <ip>` | What the forwarding engine (PFE) actually uses for a destination, not just the RIB. | operational |
| » | `show interfaces terse [<interface>]` | All interfaces with admin/link state and IP addresses. The quick overview. | operational |
| » | `show interfaces <interface> extensive` | Counters, errors, speed/duplex and the security zone of one interface. | operational |
| » | `show arp no-resolve` | The ARP table without slow DNS lookups. | operational |
| » | `show ospf neighbor / show ospf interface` | OSPF neighbors (should be Full) and the OSPF interfaces with area and cost. | operational |
| » | `show bgp summary` | BGP peers with their state and the number of active/received/accepted prefixes. | operational |
| » | `show route receive-protocol bgp <peer-ip> / show route advertising-protocol bgp <peer-ip>` | Which prefixes a BGP peer sends to you, and which you send to it. | operational |

| » | `show security flow status` | The SRX forwarding mode (flow-based or packet-based) per address family. | operational |
| » | `show security policies hit-count` | Hit counters per security policy. Shows which policy matches (or nothing matches). | operational |

## Details

### `show route <prefix> [exact] [table <instance>.inet.0]`

```
show route 10.20.30.40
show route 10.20.0.0/16 exact
show route table CORP.inet.0
```

Without `exact`, Junos shows the longest match. A `*` marks the active route; `+` is active and `-` was the last active one.


### `show interfaces terse [<interface>]`

```
show interfaces terse
show interfaces terse | match "ge-|reth"
```


### `show interfaces <interface> extensive`

```
show interfaces ge-0/0/1 extensive | match "error|drops|Speed|zone"
```


### `show ospf neighbor / show ospf interface`

Append `instance <name>` for a routing instance.


### `show bgp summary`

A number in the State column means Established (prefix counts). Active or Connect means the session is not up.


### `show route receive-protocol bgp <peer-ip> / show route advertising-protocol bgp <peer-ip>`

The received view is before the import policy. Prefixes marked hidden were rejected; see them with `show route hidden`.


### `show security flow session destination-prefix <ip> [summary]`

In flow mode (the default) every routed packet needs a session and a matching security policy. An SRX "router" still drops traffic between zones without a policy.


### `ping <ip> source <ip> [routing-instance <ri>] [rapid count <n>] [size <bytes> do-not-fragment]`

```
ping 10.20.30.40 source 10.255.0.1 rapid count 100
ping 10.20.30.40 size 1472 do-not-fragment
```


### `monitor traffic interface <interface> no-resolve matching "host <ip>"`

This only shows traffic to or from the SRX itself (control plane), not transit traffic. For transit traffic use `security flow traceoptions` or packet capture.


### `show log messages | last <n>`

```
show log messages | last 50
show log messages | match "ospf|bgp" | last 20
```


### `show configuration <section> | display set`

```
show configuration routing-options | display set
show configuration protocols bgp | display set
```


### `show | compare / commit check / commit confirmed <minutes>`

Get there: `configure`

```
configure
set routing-options static route 10.50.0.0/16 next-hop 10.255.0.2
show | compare
commit check
commit confirmed 5
commit
```

After `commit confirmed 5`, run a plain `commit` (or `commit check`) within 5 minutes, or the SRX rolls back on its own (the default is 10 minutes). `rollback 1` + `commit` restores the previous config. Show the history with `show system commit`.

> ▲ **Caution:** Always use commit confirmed for remote changes that could cut off your own access.


### `set routing-options static route <prefix> next-hop <ip>`

Get there: `configure`

```
set routing-options static route 0.0.0.0/0 next-hop 203.0.113.1
set routing-instances CORP routing-options static route 10.60.0.0/16 next-hop 10.255.10.2
```


### `show route hidden [detail]`

A prefix that a peer sends but that is missing from the routing table is usually here; `detail` shows why.


### `show interfaces diagnostics optics <interface>`

High or low warnings or alarms point to a dirty or bad fiber or a failing optic. Compare with the far end.


### `monitor interface <interface>`

Leave with q. The counters update in place, so you see whether errors are increasing right now.


### `show lldp neighbors [interface <interface>]`

If nothing shows, check that LLDP is enabled for the interface under `protocols lldp`.
